prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core approach: “Budget Responsibility Lock” – no manifesto pledge funded by extra borrowing; cut the deficit every year (OBR-verified); get debt falling and a current budget surplus ASAP. Require OBR audits of all parties’ manifestos.

Tax and spending
- Fairer taxes: restore 50p rate over £150k; introduce 10p starting rate (funded by ending Marriage Tax Allowance); no rises in basic/higher Income Tax, NI or VAT; abolish non-dom status; close avoidance loopholes; tougher HMRC culture review.
- Control welfare costs by tackling causes (low pay, housing); keep household benefit cap; no cuts to tax credits; review Universal Credit; higher JSA for long contributors.

Economy, business and work
- Productivity/industry: National Infrastructure Commission; back HS2 (keep costs down), northern rail links, roads and cycling; swift decision on airport capacity; long-term science funding.
- Green economy: decarbonise electricity by 2030; empower Green Investment Bank; Energy Security Board; 1m green jobs; robust fracking regime; support offshore sector.
- Digital: affordable high-speed broadband and wider mobile coverage; digital inclusion.
- Corporate reform: strengthen long-termism; investor duties; takeover and public interest tests; curb excessive executive pay; employee voice on pay committees; support mutuals/co-ops; keep 30% of Royal Mail public.
- Small firms: cut then freeze business rates for 1.5m properties; British Investment Bank and regional banks; more challenger banks; levy on payday lenders to boost credit unions.
- Work and pay: raise National Minimum Wage to >£8 by Oct 2019; promote Living Wage via procurement and “Make Work Pay” tax rebates; ban exploitative zero-hours (12-week regular-hours right to a contract); end agency undercutting; abolish employment tribunal fees.

Young people, skills and HE
- Guarantee an apprenticeship for every school leaver with the grades; require apprenticeships in major government contracts and large non-EU skilled recruitment; gold-standard, Level 3+ focus; create Technical Degrees.
- Cut tuition fees to £6,000 (funded by pension tax relief changes and avoidance clampdown); crack down on unpaid internships.
- Compulsory Jobs Guarantee (bank bonus tax): paid starter jobs for long-term unemployed youth (and 25+ after two years).
- Youth Allowance (18–21) tied to training.

Households and markets
- Energy: freeze bills until 2017; empower regulator to cut bills; break up Big Six generation/supply; simpler tariffs; tougher watchdog; 1m interest-free energy-efficiency loans; upgrade private rentals.
- Water: national affordability scheme; stronger regulation.
- Transport: reform franchising; allow public operator; new rail body; fares freeze next year, cap thereafter; empower regions over buses and integrated ticketing.

NHS and care
- Fund 20,000 more nurses, 8,000 GPs, 3,000 midwives (Mansion Tax, tobacco levy, anti-avoidance).
- 48-hour GP guarantee; one-week cancer tests by 2020; Cancer Treatments Fund.
- Repeal Health and Social Care Act competition; NHS preferred provider; cap private profits; protect NHS from TTIP.
- Integrate physical, mental and social care; personal care plans; parity for mental health (talking therapies within 28 days); public health action on sugar/salt/fat and cheap high-strength alcohol.
- End 15-minute care visits; recruit 5,000 home-care workers; support carers; abolish Bedroom Tax; reform Work Capability Assessment.

Education
- Protect full education budget (early years to post-16).
- Elevate technical route: Technical Baccalaureate; Institutes of Technical Education; English/Maths to 18; quality careers advice.
- All teachers qualified; Master Teacher status; School Leadership Institute; Directors of School Standards; cap KS1 classes at 30; end Free Schools waste; partnerships from private schools; compulsory age-appropriate SRE; tackle homophobic bullying.

Families, housing, communities
- Childcare: expand free hours to 25 (age 3–4, working parents); legal wraparound care 8am–6pm; double paternity leave to four weeks and raise pay.
- Build at least 200,000 homes/year by 2020; first call for local first-time buyers; “use it or lose it” on land; Future Homes Fund; garden cities; three-year tenancies with rent rise ceilings; ban letting fees; landlord register; cut homelessness.

Immigration, safety and rights
- 1,000 extra border staff; exit checks; English requirement for public-facing roles; no benefits for EU migrants until two years; ban overseas-only recruitment; extend Gangmasters Authority.
- Protect neighbourhood policing (over 10,000 officers safeguarded); Local Policing Commitment; new Police Standards Authority; victims’ law; tougher response to domestic abuse; ban legal highs.
- Counter-extremism: restore stronger controls; mandatory de-radicalisation for returnees; stronger oversight of agencies; zero-tolerance of hate crime.

Devolution, democracy, media
- Constitutional Convention; replace House of Lords with elected Senate of Nations and Regions.
- English Devolution Act: £30bn and powers to city/county regions; local Public Accounts Committees.
- Votes at 16; tougher lobbyist register; ban MPs’ paid directorships/consultancies; publish gender pay gaps; protect Human Rights Act; extend FOI; implement Leveson; protect BBC and keep Channel 4 public.

Europe and the world
- Stay in and reform the EU; single market focus; protect non-Euro members; “referendum lock” on any future power transfer.
- Defence: SDSR in year one; NATO commitment; maintain CASD nuclear deterrent; bolster cyber security; strengthen Armed Forces Covenant.
- Foreign policy: multilateralism; human rights at core; envoys for LGBT and religious freedom; two-state solution; Asia strategy.
- Climate: lead on Paris; five-year ratchets; net zero global emissions in second half of century.
- Aid: retain 0.7% GNI; focus on poorest; Centre for Universal Health Coverage; tackle tax avoidance/corruption; ethical supply chains.
